_comment: User-specified properties per MBPP task id, used by: python main.py --mode property --properties properties_example.json
17: For any non-negative side length a, the function returns 4 * a.
For side length 0, the function returns 0.
151: If the two positive integers have no common factor greater than 1 (gcd is 1), the function returns True.
If the two positive integers share a common factor greater than 1, the function returns False.
The result is symmetric: is_coprime(x, y) == is_coprime(y, x).
280: If the item is present in the list, the function returns (True, i) where i is the index of the first occurrence of the item.
If the item is not present in the list, the first element of the returned tuple is False.
For an empty list, the first element of the returned tuple is False.
492: If the item is present in the sorted list, the function returns True.
If the item is not present in the sorted list (smaller than all elements, larger than all elements, or between two elements), the function returns False.
For an empty list, the function returns False.
11: If the character does not occur in the string, the string is returned unchanged.
If the character occurs exactly once, the result is the string with that single occurrence removed.
If the character occurs two or more times, only its first and last occurrences are removed; all other characters, including middle occurrences of the character, are kept in their original order.
68: A non-decreasing list (each element >= the previous one) returns True.
A non-increasing list (each element <= the previous one) returns True.
A list that both increases and decreases somewhere returns False.
A list with zero or one element, or with all elements equal, returns True.
188: If n can be written as a*a * b*b with integers a >= 2 and b >= 2 (for example 16 = 2*2 * 2*2, 36 = 2*2 * 3*3, 144), the function returns True.
If n is the square of a prime number (for example 4, 9, 25, 49), it cannot be written with both a and b >= 2, so the function returns False (1 does not count as one of the squares).
If n is not a perfect square (for example 2, 30, 50), the function returns False.
31: The result is a list of exactly k distinct integers taken from the input lists.
The result contains the k integers that occur in the most input lists; when several integers tie for the last place, any of them may be chosen.
The result is ordered from the least frequent to the most frequent of the selected integers.
388: For n >= 1, if n is itself a power of 2, the function returns n.
For n >= 1 that is not a power of 2, the function returns the largest power of 2 strictly less than n (the result r is a power of 2, r < n and 2*r > n).
